items.title: Earl King Interview, 1980-04-10
items.q: you've got guys like Rolling Stone, Jerry Byron, Matt Rabinick, Bobby Charles, you've got a whole farm up there, we're doing it on there.

ctx.x: How did the musicians realize that?

The black records, the unity were coming into being, you had, like I was about to tell you, on the college circuit, you began to meet people, they began to talk, they began to have a certain unison with one another. Okay, defeat the capitalists, we were doing things at the time, they said, hey, this is coming too fast, and if you let it go, integration ought to be next month. This ought to be music, this is the point. So what we need is something to take the focus off of this thing right now, the pulsation of it.…

music like the Dylkans, Alciron of Combs, you had the Spades, the Corbettes, all the people were Biberino and Inferno, you know. You deal with them in groups, so I played with all of these groups at that point, you know, at one mini-gig. So, okay, we've had a chance of playing all over the rural towns, we've had a chance to feel the falsation of the people. I've even finished playing gigs when the Ku Klux Klan was taking the oars off, it was coming in the party. I've been through all of that, but it was a ball,…
